verdict.rationale: Azure's own declarative deployment tooling (Bicep and ARM templates) deploys sets of Azure resources from a single declaration. That is a first-party way to act on many resources at once, though the evidence only implies it and covers only provisioning. The CLI's scripting support is a building block for user-written loops, not a documented bulk feature, so it earns no credit. Missing for 10: documented bulk update/delete/modify operations across many items, explicit multi-resource or batch semantics, limits/error handling for bulk runs, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can perform bulk operations across many items at once

citations.quote: Bicep is a domain-specific language that uses declarative syntax to deploy Azure resources.
The template uses declarative syntax, which lets you state what you intend to deploy without having to write the sequence of programming commands to create it.
